summary: The release targets resolution of a critical memory leak in the Node.js user session service affecting 5,000 users weekly. Through comprehensive profiling, a fix will be implemented and validated under high load to restore platform reliability, reduce downtime, and enhance monitoring. Expected business outcomes include improved user retention, reduced operational overhead, and elimination of recurring maintenance windows, achieving measurable ROI through stability and customer satisfaction.
scope_overview: The scope involves root cause identification, code-level remediation in WebSocket and caching logic, 24-hour performance validation under 10,000 concurrent users, and enhanced memory monitoring with automated alerts and heap snapshots. Deliverables include leak-free code deployment, upgraded observability dashboards, and detailed RCA documentation. No infrastructure scaling or API modifications are included.
key_risks: Root cause may remain unclear after initial profiling due to transient memory allocation behaviors.
Fix could unintentionally disrupt WebSocket notification functionality or introduce backward compatibility issues.
test_readiness: Test setup is fully defined with profiling, unit, load, and end-to-end validations using clinic.js, Mocha, Postman, and k6. QA has outlined coverage goals and automation via CI/CD workflows. Staging environment readiness confirmed with Grafana integration, enabling robust verification of stability for 48 hours before production rollout.
recommendations: Prioritize extended memory profiling to conclusively isolate retention sources in WebSocket and cache layers before coding fixes.
Leverage enhanced monitoring and heap snapshot automation for proactive early detection of regressions post-release.
next_steps: Execute memory profiling and root cause identification within the first sprint day and design remediation plan.
Deploy fixed build to staging, run 48-hour validation, then proceed with rolling production release during low-traffic hours (2–4 AM EST).
